Undying flames ring the gate. Jailers drag their chains about.
A golden palace standing on clouds. Heavenly soldiers ring the throne.
Stelae with every letter erased stand like pillars of light. The swallowed names rise, each in a different form.

The address just says 'third village, during the Yellow Turban riots'. This is it, right?
The parcel keeps getting heavier. Something inside sounds like a blade being sharpened.
No deliveries to the lower floors. Last time a steel doll signed with its fist.
They say there's a time-rift surcharge. Anyone want to pay it?
The records say this village vanishes in these riots. I hope I'm wrong.
The deeper the floor, the wider the rift. Machines from my era got lost down there.
That blade looks exactly like one hanging in a museum in my time.
My way back has closed. I'll be eating this era's food for a while.
Measuring underground resonance. The readings swing wildly the deeper you go.
If you meet a sentry walker, aim for the knee joints. Straight from our field manual.
People of this era are tough. Climbing ruins without protective suits.
Bring me one sample. A floor lord's scale would be even better.

My report is due tomorrow... is there anywhere with electricity here?
Those people in gas masks look like our company's disinfection team, but they won't talk to me.
Shall I give you my card? Ah, paper is precious in this era, you say.

From my very first day the Yellow Sash mob hit the village gate. Luckily the wall held. I am Mukhyang, this village's scribe.
Something strange passed over the tiled wall - like a tiny iron eye, flying.
They call it a scout drone. A courier customer dropped his parcel and ran, and that parcel was not of this age, either.
But there is a bigger matter. Lately the names of the dead are vanishing from the steles. It began near the Burrow. First, please clear the mob at the gate.
The gate is quiet. Did you notice there was not a single letter on their spearheads? Those soldiers did not know their own names.
You said the Burrow opens just below. I will go and look at the first floor.
I reached the first floor. Name scratches ran along the wall, as if someone carved them and rubbed them out.
The rumor may be true - the Burrow is eating people's names. Continuing this record is my work. Go deeper and I will write it down.
You there, the new appointee. I am the old man who serves as drillmaster. Deal with the Black Flag bandits on the plain first. Then I will tell you about the Vow Stele.
Every night a mob under a black flag robs the plains post. Not one name is written on that flag. They say the chief's armor is studded with glowing marks.
I hear even reckless youngsters have joined the bandits. I will settle this plain first.
The Black Flag chief has fallen! Carts will roll again.
The Vow Stele is open. Enter the Vow and one death ends it, so you need resolve.
I never learned why the flag had no name. The answer must be inside the Burrow.
On the Burrow's fifth floor lies an old royal tomb. The buried soldiers are said to still stand gripping their swords. In the innermost chamber sits a jade-coffin warden.
Every wall of the tomb bore the marks of grave robbers' flashlights. Someone had come and gone before us.
I also heard of a light stele that writes new names on that wall. Please look closely.
Mister, all night there's a scraping-iron noise from the factory chimney. I'm too scared to go. But I have to go pick scrap.
They say there is an old city wall under the factory. I also heard someone in a hazmat suit has been combing the ruined city.
Yes, there are people in gray clothes! They say the factory's heart is a pipe into the Burrow. Please!
The noise stopped! The rampaging dragon is gone too. I picked up an armful of scrap.
The factory heart's pipe ran into the Burrow. It felt the same as the Burrow's name-eating sound.
I'll give you this junk shop, mister. You may need some parts.
At every ebb tide something weeps under the mudflats. Three boats have vanished. They say the sea called their names and pulled back.
A rusty observation tower stands in the middle of the flats, they say. I can see things wrapped in lab gloves, too.
Some nights a boat-song melody echoes back up from beneath the flats. The Tentacle King seems to be mimicking it.
The tide has returned with its own voice. Please take a sack of salt.
The names the flats were calling turned out to be those of the three boats' boatmen. Now those names will not stay in the Burrow.
The rumor is that the Ashen Castellan cannot leave his castle because he lost his name. Go down to floor 10.
What... was my name? For hundreds of years I have stood before a gate where only an emergency lamp blinks. Who planted this mechanical eye inside my helm?
I found the lord's name in my records. If you give it back the ghost will leave the castle, but if you seal the name the castle will give up his armor.
Whether to return the name or seal it - I will decide.
What will you do with the lord's name?
Now I remember. Hearing that name called mine, my chest feels light. I shall leave the castle. I leave my blessing with you.
One name has come back. You have recovered one of the names the Burrow swallowed.
My name is taken... but the armor that guards the castle remains. Take this fragment.
I will note the sealed name separately in my records. Whatever you decide, the record remains.
I am the wandering exorcist Soyeon. The rift is a side branch of the Nameless Hole. The gatekeeper Geomok guards that gate and filters names.
A bus had fallen into the rift. Nobody inside, and guests from a sea of stars clung to every window.
Guests from other eras. Whenever the gate opens, things of other times slip in. Deal with the gatekeeper in front of the seal stele.
New letters are carved on the seal stele. The rift has stopped, and the talisman dungeon can be opened. Please take this talisman.
There was no name on the gatekeeper's spearhead either. Even the name Geomok seemed borrowed from someone.
The furnace temperature keeps rising. The power equipment runs wild, and one colossus stands motionless in the middle of the furnace. I pitched a tent by the frontier well, but it is hot every night.
So it feeds on the rift's heat and runs amok. I will drive the mob back to near the control panel.
Birds are perching on the solar panels again! The frontier has power.
I saw a pipe from the colossus's back running to the Burrow. This heat came from the Burrow as well.
There is Black Wind Stronghold on floor 15. The chieftain is said to have sold his name to buy power. Rumor says they even have radios and guns.
I also saw a security walker standing at the stronghold's gate. The bandits bought things from other eras.
The chieftain has fallen. His name had been erased before he became chieftain. The Burrow bought it.
It was not a single man's name - there was a trade in which names were sold.
Floor 20 is a dragon palace under water. Diving-gear wreckage lies scattered beneath its tiles, and half of a pressure dome remains.
I have to deal with the Scaled Gatekeeper to go deeper. I will go down.
…Give me a name. You have one, do you not? I grew up eating them. Give me a name.
Who are you! A voice from the floor. It eats names?
That is the master of the Nameless Hole. This whole Burrow was his body. We must hurry the record.
The Western road has been blocked for three months. Neither camels nor cargo return. A truck is stuck in the sand, and they say a light gate stands open in a buried ruin.
I hear a sand-sea tyrant blocks the road. I will open the caravan route first.
I hear the bells again! Let me leave you a bolt of silk. With this road open, more names will come home.
Someone has settled in the fort ruins and the cable car has stopped. The valley is cut off. Huge handprints were frozen inside the cabin.
I will get the cable car running and climb to the fort. If there is a giant, we will meet there.
The cable car is moving again! Lights are on in the valley.
The giant's body had cooling pipes driven into it. The snow on that mountain did not belong to this land.
Creak... my name is Kkik. Fallen machines vanish one by one. Someone is gathering them. I am holding on to my name tightly, so I am fine.
If a machine stood up by eating names, it must be the scrap colossus. I will go by the old watchtower.
The wasteland's machines have fallen asleep. Let me give you a handful of screws. I want to come along too. I can teach you how to protect a name.
I have a reliable companion now. Please do repairs for me in the village, too.
This is the Karmic Fire Gate on floor 25. Warning signs are stuck to the stone pillars, and the gatekeeper's mechanical arm guards the gate. Beyond it, they say, lies the heavens.
The warning sign was written in letters of some era. I fear what is beyond the gate, but I must go.
The gate is open. The Heavenly Shrine is right before us. The final act draws near.
I will keep walking until the day the names return.
The shrine's guardian has abandoned the shrine. His blade now points at us. The light has gone out on the stele, and the elevator has collapsed.
I hear the guardian was the first general to sell his name to the Nameless King. I will climb to the Golden Palace above the clouds.
The light has returned to the stele. It seems you will be the one who pacifies the Nine Provinces.
The Cloud General has fallen. Now only the one who eats names remains. The Nameless King is before us.
Welcome. The names I ate protect me in the forms of three eras - general, biker, machine. You too, give up your name.
I will take back the erased names. Returning names to the stele forest is my work.
Every name in my record is here. Let us recover them one by one.
…The names go back. The stele gains its letters again.
My name has returned, so I will join this fight. I shall leave the castle and stand at your side.
The record is complete. Every erased name on the stele has returned. You are the one who found the names.
…The names go back. The stele gains its letters again.
I kept the sealed lord's name separately in my record. We could not return every one, but most were restored.
The record remains and the Burrow is quiet. I will stay as the one who found the names.
Strange. Every name came back, yet one letter remains in a corner of the stele. It is a name in no record.
This letter was carved on the city-ruin shard, too! They say it has no owner, so there is nowhere to return it.
The ownerless name is opening a new crack under the stele. I will go deeper into the Burrow.
Creeeak - a door on floor 32 that is not on the map. The lintel has letters of the light pillar, the door leaf has moss from the stele forest.
It means one name crossed all three eras and came to stand before this door. I will record it.
I will go beyond the door and find its owner.
At Reed Ford every night there is the sound of an oar with no boat. Whoever rows has no name, so the water will not answer.
The crack has spread as far as the ferry landing. A nameless oarsman rows across the ages.
That oarsman's boat must be moored on floor 34 of the Burrow. I will go down.
Found a boat on the floor-34 shore! I scanned the letters on its prow - same strokes as the letter on the city-ruin shard.
Even my old eyes see it. That oarsman did not lose his name - he erased it himself to protect it.
Then beyond the last gate we can give the name back.
(In a small voice) Among the names I swallowed, there was one that was never swallowed. That name opened a door inside my belly.
So there was a name that tried to protect the swallowed one.
He waits beyond the door on floor 36. This time we go not to fight but to give the name back.
So there was a stele beyond the stele. Whoever carves letters on it always gains a new name, they say.
May I carve it? ...They told me the name is "the one who walked this land"!
The ownerless name has found its owner. I close the record - you are the name beyond the stele.
Alive! I am the time traveler Yeoldusi. This hole is not on our era's maps - people call it the Nameless Hole, the hole missing from the map.
A hole missing from the map? Does it have to do with whatever eats this land's names?
It does. A place whose names are erased is erased from future records too. Deeper down, its master must be gathering names.
I will record it. Act 1 ends here. Let us find the end of this land where names vanish, together.
On the first day, Yellow Sash raiders hit the village gate. Scribe Mukhyang confesses that the names of the dead are vanishing from the steles.
At the post keeper's request, take down the Black Flag chief. Even his banner bears no name.
The jade-coffin warden of the floor-5 mausoleum. The trapped time traveler Yeoldusi says, "This hole is not on any future map."
Danchu's plea - a rampaging dragon roams the stopped factory's chimney. The factory's heart is a pipe leading into the Burrow.
Something weeps under the mudflats at every ebb tide, and three boats have vanished.
On floor 10 the Castellan's ghost cannot leave because he lost his own name. Choose whether to find it in Mukhyang's records.
The gatekeeper Geomok, whom the exorcist Soyeon has been chasing - the rift is a side branch of the Nameless Hole.
The furnace temperature keeps climbing, and the machines around it run wild.
The Black Wind chieftain of floor 15 - the bandits bought their strength by selling their names.
When the Scaled Gatekeeper of floor 20 falls, a voice rises from below for the first time: "Give me a name."
The Western road has been blocked for three months. A sand-sea tyrant sits on the caravan route.
Someone has settled in the fort ruins and the cable car stopped, leaving the valley cut off.
Fallen machines vanish one by one. Someone is gathering them.
The Hellfire Gatekeeper of floor 25 - beyond the gate lies the heavens.
The Sword-Bearing Guardian - Golden Palace Above the Clouds
Finish the shrine keeper's chain, then reach the Golden Palace on floor 30. The Cloud General sold his name to the Nameless King first.
The Nameless King who eats names waits at the very bottom.
One name remains on the stele that belongs to no record, and it opens a new crack.
The New Crack at Reed Ford
Every night an oar sounds at the ford with no boat. The rower has no name, so the water will not answer.
The final gate. This time you go not to fight but to give a name back.
💬 Return to town and the story goes on
🗺️ Set foot in 「{0}」 on the big map
The first parcel I ever delivered was a box with no address. I wandered three days unable to find the recipient.
In the end I opened it, and inside was just one note that read "a heart that will be delivered to someone".
I carried that note until I came to this age. Strangely, here recipients keep showing up.
Yesterday I showed the note to the village scribe, who said "that handwriting isn't even in my records." Now it has an address!
I used to be a man who only moved by head-office directives. I came on this business trip by directive too.
But on arrival, I found the things not in the directive never stop. Like people's names being erased in the Burrow.
I folded the directive away, and the first thing I did on my own judgment was to write down one erased name.
Today the scribe entered that name in the record. It would be a single line in a report, yet it weighs on my heart like this.
My return schedule was originally three days. I was to observe this age and go back.
But observing is strange. This village changes bit by bit just as I look at it.
So I postponed the schedule. I want to see the changes through. This village isn't in my age's records.
Yesterday I stood a long time before the nameless stele in the Burrow. In my age too there is a stele in that spot - nameless.
Kept: codex, heroes and merits stay
